content:
maya_support: FYI customer FinServCo reports lots of entries in the Requests table that are not linking to any Trace View spans. They see request id `req-0a1b2c3d` with no associated spans in the dashboard.

maya_support: Repro steps provided by customer: call our API -> get 200 with request-id header -> search Console > Traces > paste request id -> Trace View shows "no trace found". They say this started after last week's deploy.

maya_support: Example headers from customer: 
```
Request-ID: req-0a1b2c3d
Service: payments
X-Client: finserv-frontend
```

jon_platform: @maya_support can you paste the raw event payload they used for ingestion? wondering if request id format changed or if our matcher regex missed the hyphen.

maya_support: customer sent a snippet of event JSON: 
```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-14T16:22:31Z","request_id":"req-0a1b2c3d","trace_id":"tr-9f8e7d6c","service":"payments","spans":[]}
```

lisa_obs: Interesting — trace_id is present but spans array is empty. Could be ingestion pipeline dropping spans downstream or a transformation that zeroes spans for certain services. Any chance the frontend switched to a new tracer version?

ram_sre: @lisa_obs adding to that, we had a config change in span-enrichment lambda last week that filters spans by service allowlist. If payments isn't in the allowlist, it might strip spans but still persist the parent request. Checking changelog...

samir_ml_oncall: I'll grep logs for the trace id on the hotpath: 
```
$ jq -c 'select(.trace_id=="tr-9f8e7d6c")' /var/log/ingest/processed-2026-03-14.ndjson | tail -n 50
# output shows request row but no span rows emitted for that trace
```

samir_ml_oncall: I also see an ERROR in the span-forwarder at 16:22:31: `SpanBatchRejected: service_not_allowed`. That aligns with ram's config change.

jon_platform: Can someone check the allowlist config in s3 config bucket? path: `s3://redwood-config/ingest/span-allowlist.yaml` Might be missing `payments`.

ram_sre: Pulling it now.

deploy-bot: deploy #svc-ingest-lambda version 2026.3.09 rolled to prod by @infra-deploy at 2026-03-09T04:12:02Z

ram_sre: Confirmed — span-allowlist.yaml was updated on 2026-03-09 and `payments` accidentally removed during a merge. I can patch and redeploy.

maya_support: Customer is seeing this across hundreds of request IDs. They asked if there's any way to backfill spans for the missing traces.

lisa_obs: Two parts: 1) fix current pipeline so new spans are accepted; 2) backfill historical spans if we have raw span backups in S3. If raw span batches were never emitted (rejected), we may not have anything to backfill. Need to verify retention.

samir_ml_oncall: Querying raw ingestion bucket: 
```
$ aws s3 ls s3://redwood-raw-spans/2026/03/14/payments/ | head
# I see span-batch-20260314T1622.json.gz present for that minute
```

samir_ml_oncall: Good news: raw batches exist for many of the affected minutes. Looks like the forwarder rejected them but raw sink captured them. Backfill feasible.

ram_sre: I'll push a config patch to add `payments` back into allowlist and trigger a rolling restart of span-forwarder. ETA ~20m.

jon_platform: For the backfill, recommend we run a one-off replay job that reads raw batches, validates span schema, and writes to span-store with original trace_id mapping. Need a short maintenance window and estimate compute.

maya_support: Customer wants timeline and asks if their dashboard counts will update.

lisa_obs: If we backfill successfully, counts and trace links should populate, but won't retroactively fix UI caches until cache TTL expires or we invalidate relevant keys. We can do targeted cache invalidation for their org id to speed it up.

samir_ml_oncall: Running a dry-run of the backfill on staging now. Using script: 
```
python tools/replay_spans.py --src s3://redwood-raw-spans/2026/03/14/payments/ --org finserv --dry-run
```

samir_ml_oncall: Dry-run shows ~18k spans referencing ~6.2k trace_ids that currently have zero spans in span-store. No schema errors.

ram_sre: Patch deployed to prod, span-forwarder now accepting `payments`. Monitoring metrics for span-drop-rate.

deploy-bot: restart svc-span-forwarder (rolling) triggered by @ram_sre

samir_ml_oncall: Starting backfill job queued on data plane. I expect initial writes to show in ~5-10 minutes for a sampling set.

lisa_obs: I'll open a dashboard to monitor counts per org and trace-link success. tagging @maya_support so you can update FinServCo.

maya_support: Thanks all. I'll tell them we're patching the pipeline, running a backfill, and will invalidate console cache for their org. Could you post a short summary and ETA when you have one? :thumbsup: 

jon_platform: Summary for customer thread: "We identified an allowlist regression that stripped spans for payments after a recent deploy. We've patched the config, restarted services, and have a backfill job running. We expect links to start appearing within 15-30 minutes; full backfill for their window ~3 hours. We'll invalidate dashboard cache for their org to accelerate visibility."

ram_sre: Monitoring: span-drop-rate dropped to ~0% after restart. Backfill write errors: 0 so far.

samir_ml_oncall: Backfill progress: 12% complete at 16:58 UTC (writing at ~200 writes/sec).

maya_support: Pushing update to customer with ETA ~3h and interim check-in in 30m.

ticket-bot: Ticket #54821 updated: status -> escalated -> in-progress. Assigned: maya_support, samir_ml_oncall, ram_sre.

maya_support: Closing thread here; will reopen if anything regresses. Thanks everyone. :pray:
